data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'k-l-th', Kalthum means 'the one who conceals or hides'. In Islamic tradition, this name is often given to babies whose parents wish to keep their birth a secret. The name Kalthum carries the meaning “The one who conceals or hides” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kalthum usually hope their child will grow to embody the one who conceals or hides and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kalthum holds a unique cultural significance as it reflects the traditional Islamic practice of concealing the birth of a child for a certain period. In some communities, this is due to superstitious beliefs that preventing the widespread knowledge of a newborn can help protect them from misfortunes or jealousy from neighbors. However, this custom is also rooted in the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) household customs, where it is narrated that he kept the news of the birth of his grandchildren Imam Hasan and Imam Hussein a secret for some time.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Kalthum holds a profound meaning as it connects to the idea of manifesting the subtle, unseen aspects of the divine. In Sufi thought, the hidden, secret dimensions of oneself and of the universe are regarded as intimately connected to the divine. In this vein, the name Kalthum can be seen as a reminder that the true essence of ourselves and of creation in its entirety is ultimately a realm of divine secrets and mysteries. It is through the veil of concealment and the active pursuit of spiritual growth that we can uncover these wondrous truths.
